newsitem.title: UK: Bradford market see lower prices for British wool.
newsitem.headline: Bradford market see lower prices for British wool.

text.p: Lower prices were paid for British wool at this week's Bradford auction, the first to be held for a month.
Declines of up to 5 pence a kg were said to be due to the sterling adjustment, and the trade was reasonably satisfied that no weakness in the crossbred wool market was being signalled.

At the merino end of the market values will be tested next week in Australia and the general impression in Bradford and Europe is that the firmer tendency at closing sales before the recess will still apply. Sydney futures prices are followed with interest, whether or not the firms involved actually trade on them and the tendency during during the past two to three weeks has been definitley firmer.

Locally holidays are the main reason given for the lack of business. If prices are mentioned at all, they are very cornpetitive indeed. Anyone with export interests, and this applies more or less to the entire industry, is increasingly worried about the rise in the sterling exchange rate.
